chunks: Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed us of it, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darrāj, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who is affected by janabah and forgets to urinate until he performs ghusl, then after the ghusl he sees something. Should he perform ghusl again? He said: No; it has been pressed out and descended from the passages.

key_terms.تَعَصَّرَتْ: it was squeezed out or pressed out
key_terms.شَيْئًا: something seen after ghusl, referring to a residual discharge
key_terms.يَبُولَ: to urinate, here referring to istibra' before ghusl
key_terms.ٱلْجَنَابَةُ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.ٱلْحَبَائِلِ: the passages or channels from which the residual matter descended
key_terms.ٱلْغُسْلِ: the ritual bath performed to remove janabah

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets to urinate before ghusl al-janabah and later sees discharge, must he repeat the ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal ruling concerning janabah and what is seen after ghusl when one had forgotten to urinate beforehand. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that seeing something afterward does not require repeating the ghusl, as it is understood to be residual matter discharged from the passages.
